name: Haas ST-25 turning centre
about: Links from Haas's ST-20/25 STEP (moonshot/library/stations/extract.py; bounds, volumes and inertias in st25.links.json), in a world frame with the floor at z = 0, the spindle's axis along +X at y = 0 and z = 1005.2 (Haas's layout drawing: about 39.4 in, 1,000 mm), the operator at -Y: the headstock at the left, the turret at the right. Joint zero is the STEP's pose: X and Z at home (their + ends), the door closed, the probe arm stowed; the chucks' jaws fully open. Sources: spec is Haas's ST-25 page (haascnc.com, read 2026-11-06); layout is Haas's ST-20/25 layout drawing (st-20-25(2-axis)_layout_drawing_2020-10.pdf); manual is Haas's 2023 Lathe Operator's Manual (english_lathe_interactive_manual_print_version_2023.pdf) and, where it says so, the Haas Factory Outlet's NGC lathe manual (Haas-NGC-Lathe-Operator-with-VPS-8-2022.pdf); cad is measured on the STEP; kitagawa and royal are the chucks' makers (kitagawa.global BR10; royalproducts.com 42057 and its instructions R220001 rev D). Downloads are in C:/jigged-data/originals/machines/st25/docs and workholding/c5/docs.
gaps: The tailstock is Haas's option (spec: not in the standard build; layout: 11.9-32.9 in from the spindle face) and the shop's G2 parts are short: not fitted, so no tailstock joint and no TS keys acting
The BR10's STEP has its master jaws merged into its body, so they are drawn with the body: only the soft jaws (with their T-nuts and bolts) move, 4.4 mm at most

The Z way covers are telescopic in the machine; here they are drawn fixed where the STEP has them, so the saddle passes into the left one as Z runs toward the chuck (look only: nothing collides with them)
A collet pulls the bar back a little as it closes (a pullback chuck); here its fingers close only radially
The spindle's own rotating parts behind the nose (its tube and rotary cylinder) are drawn with the base; only the nose ring, the drawtube and the chuck turn in the render

The drawtube's pull is applied at the jaws (or the collet's fingers) through the wedge's or the taper's ratio, the drawtube and piston's 5.8 kg as the jaws' reflected inertia and the oil's flow as their damping: the drawtube itself, touching nothing inside the headstock, is shown following them by the ratio rather than simulated (tied to them, its 4-6x lever made the jaws' stops and contacts too soft to hold 10-20 kN)
The turret's clamp and unclamp before an index are folded into its index time

The foot pedal's press: the body model has no legs, so a foot on the pedal is an input to the control (Control.press_pedal), the pedal's own spring and switch simulated for anything else that presses it

masses_source.reason: The door is its CAD volume (3,892 cm3) as steel, its window counted as steel. Haas gives the machine's 9,000 lb, not its links': the saddle, X slide and turret disc are their CAD castings priced well under solid (filled in the STEP, as the band saw's), and only set inertia, as the axes are position servos. The drawtube is its CAD volume as steel; the probe arm its arm and stylus with the motor's rotor

z.reason: Haas ST-25: Z 22.50 in (572 mm), rapids 945 ipm (24.0 m/min); home at the + end, away from the chuck (manual: the axes home to their + limits)

x.reason: Haas ST-25: X 8.40 in (213 mm), rapids 945 ipm; home at the + end, away from the spindle's axis
x.axis_reason: Square to the spindle on the slant bed, 55 deg up from horizontal toward the back: the X and Z rails' faces (50-0044_01, 50-0044_02) have the normal (0, 0.574, 0.819) in the STEP; the turret's centre stands on this line through the spindle's axis, 456.8 mm out at home

turret.reason: The BOT turret's 12 faces in the STEP, its axis parallel to the spindle's through its centre; station 1 faces the spindle at joint zero
turret.speed_reason: Haas gives no index time; a used-machine dealer's ST-25 listing gives 1 second, taken as the turret's farthest index (180 deg, the shorter way round); the turret's clamp and unclamp folded in

spindle.reason: Haas ST-25: 3,400 rpm, 300 ft-lbf (407 N m) at 500 rpm, belt drive; A2-6 nose, whose face is at x = 39.7 where Haas's own chucks seat in the STEP
spindle.rotor_reason: The spindle's own turning parts (its tube, nose, drawtube, rotary cylinder: about 16,000 cm3 of steel in the STEP, 80-115 mm in radius) as about 0.35 kg m2; the chuck's own inertia is added to it

drawtube.reason: The ST-25's drawtube: 2.75 in (69.8 mm) from the spindle face extended, 1.615 in (41.0 mm) retracted, a 28.8 mm stroke; positive draws it back (the chucks close on it, OD clamping)
drawtube.damping_reason: The rotary cylinder's oil flow: at 10 kN of draw the BR10 closes its 19 mm stroke in about 0.4 s

door.reason: The door slides toward the headstock on its track (Door Track, x -747.5 to 751.1 in the STEP): to its end, its right edge stops at x = 61.6, clear of the chuck's jaws
door.friction_reason: A 30 kg door on rollers: a 20 N pull starts it, as the VF-2's lighter doors take 15 N

probe_arm.reason: The automatic tool presetter (Haas's option; M104/M105): its arm ('tre') turns on a hub 95 mm across about an axis along X (the cylinders r 47.6 and 23.2 in the STEP), on the motor housing below the spindle at the headstock wall. The STEP has it stowed round the chuck, its stylus under the tip guard; extended, it turns 84.2 deg, the angle that brings the stylus's centre into the plane the tools move in (solved on the STEP's hub axis and stylus: stowed, the stylus stands 232 mm out of that plane), the stylus then at x = 406.7, 47.8 mm out from the spindle's axis along X and 223 mm in front of the jaws
probe_arm.time_reason: Haas gives no time for the arm: about 1.5 s each way

br10.name: Kitagawa BR10 10 in 3-jaw hydraulic power chuck
br10.reason: BR10: jaw stroke 8.8 mm on the diameter, plunger stroke 19 mm, max draw bar pull 49 kN for 123 kN of static grip (OD), 4,500 rpm, 35.8 kg with soft top jaws, 0.32 kg m2. Its wedge closes the jaws 4.4 mm for the plunger's 19, an ideal 4.32 of grip per unit of pull: Kitagawa's own 2.51 is that less the wedge's friction, taken as a constant efficiency (0.581). Soft jaws SB10B1 from its STEP (UC, fully open), 40 mm wide, 42 long, their faces 183.5 out; steel, 1.40 kg each with T-nut and bolts
br10.soft_jaw_bore_reason: Soft jaws are bored to each part with the jaws near mid-stroke (2.2 mm closed), so a part of the bore's size is gripped 2.2 mm in and an open jaw stands 2.2 mm clear of it

c5.name: Royal 42057 low-profile pullback CNC collet chuck, 5C, A2-6
c5.reason: 42057: the collet drawn into the chuck to close and pushed out to open by the lathe's drawtube (a drawtube adapter it ships with); max drawbar 4,490 lbf (19,972 N), max clamping 15,750 lbf (70,059 N), 6,000 rpm, 19 lb, the nose 2.63 in across and 6.00 in long overall: on the A2-6 its nose stands at x = 192.1. A 5C collet's 10 deg half-angle closes it radially 0.176 mm a mm of draw, an ideal 5.67 of grip per unit of pull; Royal's 3.51 is that less the taper's friction (0.619). Its inertia is its CAD's at the weight's density
c5.collet_reason: No collet record gives a 5C's open and closed bore: open, 0.4 mm over its 5/8 in on the diameter, so a bar slides in; closed on nothing, 0.4 mm under, its range; the grip 25 mm long, the face flush with the nose; 0.25 kg

turret.reason: BOT tool layout (page 6): at X home an OD tool's tip is 6.50 in (165.1 mm) from the spindle's centre and 0.25 in (6.35 mm) in front of the turret's face, an ID tool's axis 7.04 in (178.8 mm) from it: from the turret's centre, 456.8 mm out on the X line (cad), 291.7 and 278.0 mm. Station k is (k - 1) x 30 deg round from station 1, which faces the spindle at joint zero; TURRET FWD brings the next

headstock_wall.reason: The front bulkhead (cad), the work area's left wall; the spindle's nose comes through it

trough_front.reason: The chip guard sloping from the door's sill down into the conveyor's trough (cad, section at x = 250)

trough_floor.reason: The chip conveyor's trough under the spindle (cad): a parted part lands here, 630 mm under the axis

trough_back.reason: The trough's back slope toward the bed (cad)

door_sill.reason: The tray under the door (cad, door tray1 and front tray)

front_right.reason: The enclosure's front right of the door opening (cad)

door_panel.reason: The door's front, its window in it (cad: the door's sheet at y -295 to -290, its lip to -309)

door_roof.reason: The door's top, wrapping back over the work area (cad)

door_pull.reason: The door's pull bar (22-8895 in the STEP): a 1-1/4 in tube, vertical at x 686.2, 64 mm proud of the door on two bends; its collider the tube as a vertical cylinder

pendant_face.reason: The thin pendant's face (cad, y -431 at its face)

estop.reason: The CAD's button above the jog handle, 31.5 mm across, 19.8 mm proud: the E-stop on Haas's thin pendant

cycle_start_button.reason: proposed: the CAD's thin pendant draws no Cycle Start; placed as on the VF-2's NGC pendant, left of Feed Hold 110.5 mm under the jog handle's centre, 31.5 mm across, 10 mm proud

feed_hold_button.reason: proposed: as Cycle Start, to its right

stylus.reason: The presetter's stylus head (kj in the STEP), stowed

probe_arm.reason: The arm's curved tube, 38 mm across, round the chuck's front from its hub to the stylus head, as three capsules on its centreline (cad: its sections every 30 mm in height); stowed, it stands 180 mm or more from the spindle's axis, clear of the 10 in chuck

door_handle.reason: The pull bar's middle, gripped round at chest height and pulled toward the headstock to open

jog_handle.reason: The CAD's dial, 60 mm across, its face 16.5 mm proud of the pendant inside a 80 mm bezel, with a spinner knob 25.6 mm under its centre standing 16.5 mm proud of it; at_mm is the face's centre. 100 clicks a turn, the detent and damping as the VF-2's [proposed]; a positive turn is clockwise as the operator sees it, which jogs +

keys.reason: proposed: the CAD's keyboard under the screen is flat, so the keys are the VF-2's NGC layout (moonshot/library/stations/vf2.json) moved onto this pendant (x + 235, z - 105), the lathe's own keys in the mill's places: X DIAMETER MEASURE, NEXT TOOL, X/Z and Z FACE MEASURE for TOOL OFFSET MEASURE, NEXT TOOL, TOOL RELEASE and PART ZERO SET; HANDLE SCROLL, ATC FWD (turret forward) and ATC REV in the MDI row; +X, -X, +Z, -Z, JOG LOCK and the tailstock's keys in the jog cluster; FWD, STOP and REV in the overrides' place, under the numbers (manual 4.4-4.7)

pedal.reason: proposed: Haas's chuck foot pedal (manual 1.2, Lathe - Features: 7. Foot Pedal; TG0066: clamp and unclamp) isn't in the STEP: a common foot switch, its pad 150 x 200 mm hinged at the heel and raised 8 deg toward the toe, on the floor in front of the machine under the door's left half, by the operator's right foot. It springs back up (2 N m held against its stop, 20 N m a radian: about 45 N at the pad's middle to press it 8 deg, where its switch closes); each closing toggles the chuck (TG0066: the input toggles when pressed)

affordances_source.reason: The door's handle is the CAD's pull bar; the E-stop and jog handle are measured on the CAD's pendant (2026-11-06); the buttons and keys as noted

interlocks: with the door open, in Run or Setup mode, Cycle Start, the spindle's FWD and REV, a turret index and the probe arm are refused, the chuck clamps and unclamps (manual 3.5)
with the door open, handle jog works only in Setup mode (manual 3.5)
the door is locked closed while a program runs, the spindle turns or an axis moves; it unlocks when the machine isn't in cycle (manual 3.5)
the chuck won't unclamp while the spindle turns faster than Setting 283 (Haas Setting 283)
Cycle Start and the spindle are refused with the chuck unclamped (Haas Setting 284, off)
the foot pedal toggles the chuck; M10 clamps and M11 unclamps (Haas M10/M11, TG0066); M104 extends and M105 retracts the probe arm (Haas M104/M105)
with the probe arm extended, a tool touching its stylus stops the axis and writes the tool's offset (HFO manual: press -X until the probe beeps; movement stops)

unclamp_source.reason: Setting 283's value isn't in the manual; set to 0 here: the chuck opens only with the spindle stopped

clamp_source.reason: The chuck's pressure is set per job ('hydraulic pressure must be set correctly to securely hold the work piece without distortion', manual 3.2): a job's takes give their own; 10 kN of draw, a fifth of the BR10's 49 kN, when none does

jog_source.reason: Manual 4.5: each increment key's bottom number sets the speed when an axis jog key is held (.0001/.1, .001/1, .01/10, .1/100)

x_jog_source.reason: The manual doesn't say whether a click of X moves the tool its increment on the radius or the diameter: here the radius, as the axis moves
